name: Northmarch
seat: Greyspire (pass-fortress at the Stone Crown's southern shoulder)
summary: The human frontier of the highlands: one long valley of pass-forts, lead- and silver-mines, and hard bargains. Northmarch exists because somebody must hold the passes between the Crownlands and the deep-folk realm — and because the ore is good.

government.title: Warden-Earl
government.note: The earldom swears to the Velkash Crown in theory; in practice the passes answer to whoever keeps them open.

laws: Crown law, lightly — the March keeps its own pass-code: tolls, weights, and mine-safety are sworn on iron. Glimmerborn are reported south per the Accords, when anyone remembers to.

relations.note: Ore-weight honesty is the whole relationship.
The March sells no Greenwood timber and says so loudly.

history_notes: Chartered after the Rebuilding to hold the passes no army had held since the Sundering.
Deep-Shapers sealed a ringing shaft in a March mine last spring; Earl Maren's questions went unanswered.
adventure_hooks: A leased dwarf mine breaks through into something that rings; both realms seal it and both hire players to watch the other's seal.
Silver shipments vanish between pass-forts; the only witness is a Glimmerborn goatherd the Accords require be surrendered.
The Warden-Earl invites players to a feast and an inquisition: someone in Greyspire sold pass-keys to the ash-barons.
